_note: Core/Handoff (F17.8) — the platform-neutral corpus for continuity. The real constraint is a SIZE LIMIT nobody documents precisely: Apple transports an NSUserActivity's userInfo over Bluetooth LE advertisement plus a short exchange, and an oversized payload does not error — the activity simply stops appearing on the other device, and the developer has nothing to debug. A limit only one platform enforces, or two measure differently, is not a limit. So the payload grammar, the CANONICAL serialisation and the byte count are decided here. The canonical form is deliberately exact: ASCII sorted keys (Swift's default String ordering is Unicode-canonical and would sort differently from JS and Kotlin), integers only (a binary float has no single decimal spelling), and hand-written escapes rather than each platform's JSON encoder. Read by kernel/test/handoff-conformance.test.ts (TS, reference), :core HandoffConformanceTest (Kotlin) and Engine/iOS/Handoff.swift. Byte counts were produced by an independent UTF-8 derivation, never by the code under test.

activityType.name: hyphens are legal in a label
case is preserved — Apple matches NSUserActivityTypes exactly
a trailing dot leaves an empty label
an underscore is not a DNS character

url.name: absent is legal — a fallback is optional
the scheme folds for the check but the URL is kept verbatim
a custom scheme opens nothing on a Mac that never installed the app
a bare host is not a URL

canonical.name: keys are SORTED, not authored-order — three languages must produce one string
every scalar kind plus one array
a two-byte character counts as two
a three-byte character counts as three
an astral character counts as four, not two UTF-16 units
a newline is escaped short-form, which is one byte cheaper than \u000a
a fractional number has no single decimal spelling, so it is refused
a non-ASCII key would sort differently in Swift than in JS and Kotlin
a nested object — a handoff payload is a pointer to state, not the state

activity.name: no payload is an empty one, not an error
a payload that is an array rather than an object
a fractional number in the payload

oversize._note: Built at test time rather than written out: a 3 KB literal in a corpus is unreadable and would drift from the constant. The runner fills `key` with `filler` repeated until the canonical form crosses the ceiling.

continuation.name: what arrives is normalised into the shape the sender advertised
a malformed incoming URL is DROPPED, not refused — losing the whole handoff over a bad fallback is worse
a missing payload arrives as an empty one
